name: Soil Health Card (Free Soil Testing)
summary: A free soil test for your field and a card that tells you exactly which nutrients your soil needs, so you buy only the fertilizer you need.

benefits.headline: Free soil test and crop-wise fertilizer recommendation
details: Your soil is tested free of cost at a government laboratory for 12 parameters (nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, sulphur, micronutrients, pH, organic carbon and more).
The card gives crop-wise fertilizer and soil-amendment advice, which helps cut input cost and avoid overuse.
Cards are issued again after about two years so you can see how your soil is changing.

summary: Every farmer is eligible, whether a small, marginal or large landholder.
You need legal access to cultivable land (owned or leased).
A soil sample from your field is collected and tested; there is no fee.

steps: Contact your block/district Agriculture office, Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) or nearest soil testing lab and ask for soil sampling in your field.
A sample is collected from your field (usually after the Rabi or Kharif harvest, before the next crop is sown). Give the correct plot details.
The sample is tested at a soil testing laboratory.
Collect your printed Soil Health Card, or view and download it on the portal using your details. Follow the fertilizer advice for your crop.

deadline.text: No deadline. The best time to get your soil sampled is right after harvest, before you sow the next crop.

caveats: The scheme is now run under RKVY 'Soil Health & Fertility', so the way sampling is organised differs from state to state.
